title: How do we draw the height of a corner of a triangle?
description: The height of a corner is the straight drop to the opposite side. A ruler and a set square draw it: the ruler stays on the base, the set square slides until its upright edge touches the corner, and the line is drawn. Keeko's doubt is that any line to the base will do.
teaching_notes: One idea: an altitude is the line from a corner that meets the opposite side at a right angle, and the set square slid along the base draws it. Watch for students who join the corner to the middle of the base.

source: Let AD be the line segment from A drawn perpendicular to BC. The length of AD is the height of the vertex A from BC. The line segment AD is said to be one of the altitudes of the triangle. Construct the altitude from A to BC. Constructing the altitude using just a ruler is not accurate. To get a more precise angle of 90°, we use a set square along with a ruler. Step 1: Keep the ruler aligned to the base. Place the set square on the ruler as shown, such that one of the edges of the right angle touches the ruler. Step 2: Slide the set square along the ruler till the vertical edge of the set square touches the vertex A. Step 3: Draw the altitude to BC through A using the vertical edge of the set square.
video_script.why: The child knows what a perpendicular is and now draws the height of a corner of a triangle with a ruler and a set square.
video_script.substitution: A triangle ABC with its base BC, a ruler and a set square.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC standing on its base BC, with a ruler along the base and a set square on the ruler
video_script.wrong_answer: any line from the corner to the base is an altitude
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko joins the corner to the middle of the base with a slanting line and calls it the altitude, but the altitude must meet the base at a right angle.
video_script.payoff_line: The line eigh dee is the altitude from eigh

final_answer.value: AD, the perpendicular from A to BC, is the altitude from A; its length is the height
final_answer.spoken: the line eigh dee is the altitude from eigh, and its length is the height

hold_back: AD is the altitude from A
maths_rules: the ruler stays along the base BC and the set square rests on it with one edge of its right angle against the ruler
sliding the set square along the ruler keeps its upright edge at a right angle to BC
the line drawn along the upright edge from A to BC is AD, and ∠ADB = ∠ADC = 90°
AD is the altitude from A, and its length is the height of A from BC
video_script.design: The triangle stays on the board with the ruler along the base. The set square slides along the ruler, and the line drawn along its upright edge ends at the foot D on the base.
